sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **Introduction to Object-Oriented Thinking**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Thinking in objects
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **Introduction to Object-Oriented Thinking** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Object-oriented thinking models problems by identifying objects, their data, and operations
Procedural programming organizes code into functions; OOP organizes it into classes and objects
Identify classes by looking for nouns in the problem description
Identify methods by looking for verbs and actions associated with each noun
OOP promotes code reuse, flexibility, and easier maintenance of large programs

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Introduction to Object-Oriented Thinking - Thinking in objects. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: What is the key difference between procedural and object-oriented programming?
options: OOP organizes code around objects with data and behavior, procedural around functions
questions.explanation: Procedural programming focuses on functions/procedures operating on data, while OOP organizes code around objects that combine data (fields) and behavior (methods) together.

questions.question: What does 'thinking in objects' mean when designing a program?
options: Identifying real-world entities and modeling them as classes with properties and behaviors
questions.explanation: Thinking in objects means identifying real-world entities relevant to the problem and modeling them as classes with appropriate data fields (properties) and methods (behaviors).
